slice: Pass 7: 2024 Yamaha YZ250FX (US owner's service manual BAJ-2819U-14, tests, known issues)

records.statement: Yamaha's US owner's service manual for the 2024 YZ250FX identifies it as model YZ250FXR, model code(s) BAJL; the manual is the US-market edition (Yamaha part BAJ-2819U-14).
records.notes: Designation suffix letter is Yamaha's model-year code. Market editions for other regions carry other model codes.

records.statement: The 2024 YZ250FX engine is a liquid-cooled 250 cm³ DOHC four-stroke single, bore × stroke 77.0 × 53.6 mm (3.03 × 2.11 in), compression ratio 13.8 : 1, electric start, wet-sump lubrication.

Fuel injection with throttle body ID B7B1; fuel line pressure at idle 300–390 kPa (3.0–3.9 kgf/cm², 43.5–56.6 psi), idle speed 1900–2100 r/min; valve clearance (cold) intake 0.12–0.19 mm (0.0047–0.0075 in), exhaust 0.17–0.24 mm (0.0067–0.0094 in).
Engine control unit BAJ2; TCI ignition with timing 8.0–12.0 /2000 r/min; fuel pump and electronic fuel injection.

records.topic: 2024 YZ250FX maps, Power Tuner and launch control
records.statement: On the US 2024 YZ250FX a handlebar switch toggles map 1 (all-around power and response) and map 2 (milder throttle response for technical sections); the Power Tuner smartphone app connects over the CCU (Communication Control Unit) wireless network to adjust the maps and settings.

KYB coil-spring fork, 310 mm (12.2 in) travel, Yamaha Suspension Oil S1, 501.0 cm³ (16.94 US oz, 17.67 Imp.oz) per leg; standard clickers (counted out from fully in): rebound 12 of 20, compression 12 of 20.

KYB link shock, 317 mm (12.5 in) wheel travel; standard settings: spring preload 6.0 mm (0.24 in) turned in from free length, rebound 11 clicks out (of 30), high-speed compression 1-1/8 turns out, low-speed compression 11 clicks out.

Standard spring rates are 4.6 N/mm (fork) and 56 N/mm (shock); Yamaha lists optional fork springs from 4.1-5.1 N/mm. Rear sag is set to a sunken (rider-on) length of 90-100 mm before any other tuning.
records.notes: Spring tables in the Tuning chapter (front fork / rear shock absorber setting parts).

records.statement: Constant mesh 6-speed; primary reduction 3.353 (57/17); gear ratios 1st 2.385 (31/13), 2nd 1.813 (29/16), 3rd 1.444 (26/18), 4th 1.143 (24/21), 5th 0.957 (22/23), 6th 0.815 (22/27); secondary (final) reduction 3.923 (51/13), i.e. stock sprockets 13T front / 51T rear, chain final drive.

Wet multi-disc clutch: 2 pcs friction plate 1 (2.70–2.90 mm), 6 pcs friction plate 2 (2.72–2.88 mm), 7 pcs clutch plate (1.50–1.70 mm); clutch spring free length 44.50 mm (1.75 in); 520 sealed type chain, 114 links, slack 50.0–60.0 mm (1.97–2.36 in). Yamaha lists optional rear sprockets of 47, 48, 49, 50, 51, 52 teeth.
records.notes: Plate counts are listed in manual order (friction plate types first, then clutch/steel plates).

records.topic: 2024 YZ250FX overall gear ratios and speed per 1,000 rpm
records.statement: Worked out from Yamaha's ratios, overall reduction (engine to rear wheel) is 1st 31.37:1, 2nd 23.85:1, 3rd 18.99:1, 4th 15.03:1, 5th 12.59:1, 6th 10.72:1; on the stock 110/100-18 rear tire that is about 1st 4.07 km/h, 2nd 5.35 km/h, 3rd 6.72 km/h, 4th 8.49 km/h, 5th 10.14 km/h, 6th 11.91 km/h per 1,000 rpm.

source.name: BAK calculation from Yamaha 2024 YZ250FX OSM ratios

records.notes: overall = primary 3.353 x gear x secondary 3.923. Speed = rpm / overall x tire circumference; nominal rolling diameter 677 mm from 110/100-18 (rim x 25.4 + 2 x section x aspect), circumference 2.127 m, no tire squat or growth.

records.statement: Worked out from Yamaha's gearbox and stock sprockets: first gear gives about 4.07 km/h and top gear about 11.91 km/h per 1,000 rpm, so at 10,000 rpm first runs out near 41 km/h and top near 119 km/h (74 mph). The ratio between first and top gear is 2.93, a measure of how wide the box is.

source.name: BAK calculation from Yamaha 2024 YZ250FX OSM ratios

records.notes: Reference rpm 10000 chosen as a typical working rpm, not a published rev limit. Same tire assumptions as the drivetrain record.

records.statement: Caster angle 27.2 °, trail 116 mm (4.6 in), wheelbase 1480 mm (58.3 in), seat height 955 mm (37.6 in), ground clearance 320 mm (12.60 in), overall length 2175 mm (85.6 in).

Curb weight 111 kg (245 lb); fuel tank 8.2 L (2.2 US gal, 1.8 Imp.gal) with 2.0 L (0.53 US gal, 0.44 Imp.gal) reserve; tires 80/100-21 51M front and 110/100-18 64M rear (DUNLOP/MX33F / DUNLOP/MX33), 100 kPa (15 psi) standard pressure.

Engine oil 10W-40, 10W-50, 15W-40, 20W-40 or 20W-50 (API service SG type or higher, JASO standard MA), 0.73 L (0.77 US qt, 0.64 Imp.qt) at a change, 0.75 L (0.79 US qt, 0.66 Imp.qt) with filter, 0.95 L (1.00 US qt, 0.84 Imp.qt) dry; coolant 0.93 L (0.98 US qt, 0.82 Imp.qt); spark plug NGK/LMAR8E-J gapped 0.6–0.7 mm (0.024–0.028 in).

records.topic: 2024 YZ250FX valve clearance and top end
records.statement: Valve clearance (cold) intake 0.12–0.19 mm (0.0047–0.0075 in), exhaust 0.17–0.24 mm (0.0067–0.0094 in); cylinder bore 77.000–77.010 mm (3.0315–3.0319 in) (wear limit 77.060 mm (3.0339 in)); piston-to-cylinder clearance 0.030–0.055 mm (0.0012–0.0022 in).

Yamaha's tuning chart for this model says: set rear sag (sunken length 90-100 mm) first; if the fork is stiff over its whole range back the compression out about 2 clicks, take 5-10 cc of oil out or fit a softer spring; if it is soft and bottoms, add about 2 clicks of compression or 5-10 cc of oil, or fit a stiffer spring; change oil in 5 cc steps for end-of-stroke feel. After a softer spring go 1-2 clicks out on rebound, after a stiffer one 1-2 clicks in.
records.notes: From the Tuning chapter (front fork setting / suspension setting tables) of this manual.

records.statement: Yamaha's troubleshooting chart for the 2024 YZ250FX traces hard starting, poor idle and poor mid-to-high-speed running to: a clogged or failing fuel pump, a failed or clogged injector, a blocked tank-cap breather, stale or contaminated fuel, wrong valve timing, valve clearance out of spec, a bent or stuck valve, a tired or broken valve spring, a worn cam lobe, a dirty throttle body, a cracked throttle-body joint (air leak), engine oil overfilled, the wrong oil grade letting the starter clutch slip, besides ignition faults (no spark).

causes_listed: a clogged or failing fuel pump
a tired or broken valve spring
the wrong oil grade letting the starter clutch slip

records.notes: Troubleshooting chapter (TROUBLESHOOTING OF ENGINE). Yamaha notes the chart is a quick-reference guide and does not cover every cause.

records.topic: 2024 YZ250FX Yamaha clutch, gearbox and cooling troubleshooting
records.statement: Yamaha's 2024 YZ250FX troubleshooting chart lists clutch slip from worn friction plates, tired clutch springs, oil too thin, old oil; clutch drag from swollen friction plates, warped steel plates, oil too thick, a seized clutch-housing bushing; jumping out of gear from bent or worn shift forks, a worn shift-drum groove, worn gear dogs, a weak stopper-lever spring; and overheating from low coolant, a faulty radiator cap, clogged or bent radiator fins, a faulty water pump, carbon build-up in the combustion chamber, a dragging brake, the wrong plug heat range.

overheating: carbon build-up in the combustion chamber

records.notes: Troubleshooting chapter (clutch, transmission and cooling system tables).

records.statement: With the Yamaha diagnostic tool connected to the 2024 YZ250FX, diagnostic code 01 shows the throttle angle, 11–14 fully closed and 86–92 fully open; code 08 shows the lean-angle sensor output, 0.4–1.4 V upright and 3.7–4.4 V overturned (fault code 30 is set when the bike has overturned); code 60 reports any Power Tuner fuel-injection or ignition-timing correction stored in the ECU's EEPROM, and codes 64/65 show and erase the Power Tuner setting history.
records.notes: SELF-DIAGNOSTIC FUNCTION AND DIAGNOSTIC CODE TABLE (sensor operation table).

records.topic: 2024 YZ250FX valve train and crank dimensions
records.statement: Yamaha lists for the 2024 YZ250FX: intake cam lobe height limit 32.130 mm (1.2650 in) and exhaust 33.460 mm (1.3173 in); valve stem diameter limit 4.945 mm (0.1947 in) intake, 4.430 mm (0.1744 in) exhaust; valve spring free length limit 34.94 mm (1.38 in) intake, 33.82 mm (1.33 in) exhaust; crank assembly width 55.93–56.00 mm (2.202–2.205 in).
records.notes: Engine maintenance specifications. Where the manual prints only a wear limit, the figure is that limit.

records.statement: Spoked wheels with 21 x 1.60 front and 18 x 2.15 rear rims; hydraulic single-disc brakes front and rear (master cylinder bore 9.52 mm (0.37 in) front, 11.0 mm (0.43 in) rear).

Replace at these 2024 YZ250FX wear limits: clutch friction plate 2.60 mm (0.102 in); drive chain 15-link length 239.3 mm (9.42 in); brake pad lining 1.0 mm (0.04 in); brake disc thickness 2.5 mm (0.10 in) front, 3.5 mm (0.14 in) rear.

Yamaha offers 2024 YZ250FX rear sprockets of 47T, 48T, 49T, 50T, 51T, 52T (standard 51T; front 13T) and advises a lower final ratio (fewer rear teeth) for courses with long straights and a higher one for courses with many corners, set by riding the whole circuit on the day.
records.notes: Tuning chapter, SELECTION OF THE SECONDARY REDUCTION RATIO (SPROCKET) and setting-parts table (part numbers in values).

records.topic: 2024 YZ250FX what a sprocket change does
records.statement: Worked out from the 2024 YZ250FX stock 13/51 gearing: each rear tooth changes every gear by about 2.0% and one front tooth by about 7.7% (one front tooth is roughly 3.9 rear teeth). Yamaha's 47T to 52T rear range spans final ratios 3.615 to 4.000 (stock 3.923), so the 47T gives about +8.5% road speed per rpm in every gear and the 52T about -1.9%: more teeth means shorter gearing, quicker pull and a lower top speed.

source.name: BAK calculation from Yamaha 2024 YZ250FX OSM sprocket table

records.notes: Percent per tooth = 1/teeth; final ratio = rear/front teeth.

records.statement: Yamaha's 2024 lineup announcement lists the YZ250FX among the cross-country models that return for 2024 with updated graphics and a new seat color; unlike the 2024 YZ250F it received no engine or frame update, so it keeps the previous-generation YZ250FX engine and chassis.

source.name: Yamaha Motor Corporation USA press release "Yamaha Celebrates 50 Years of YZ" (2024 lineup)

records.notes: The spec tables of the 2022 (BAJ-2819U-12), 2023 (BAJ-2819U-13) and 2024 (BAJ-2819U-14) US owner service manuals were compared: engine, gearing, suspension and chassis figures are identical (only a clutch friction-plate wear limit differs, 2.60 vs 2.62 mm, and text formatting).

records.statement: A rear-wheel dyno test of the 2022 YZ250FX, mechanically identical to the 2024, measured 37.9 hp at 12,100 rpm and 18.3 lb-ft of torque at 8,800 rpm; peak power was up only 0.1 hp on the 2021 bike, with peak torque the same but arriving 400 rpm later.

source.name: Dirt Rider, 2022 Yamaha YZ250FX Dyno Test (Andrew Oldar)

records.notes: Tested bike is a 2022. Applied to 2024 because Yamaha says the 2024 FX carries over with graphics only and the 2022-2024 manual spec tables match (see identity record). Dyno model and map not stated; in-house dyno, rear street tire. No dyno test of a 2023 or 2024 FX was found.

records.topic: 2024 YZ250FX tire pressure and fork oil level by conditions
records.statement: Yamaha's tuning chapter sets standard tire pressure at 100 kPa (15 psi), dropping to 60-80 kPa (9-12 psi) for rain, mud, sand or slippery ground and raising it to 100-120 kPa (15-18 psi) for stony or hard ground to avoid flats. The fork's end-of-stroke (air spring) feel is tuned with the oil level: standard 295 cm³, adjustable from 260 to 365 cm³ in 5 cm³ steps; too little gives a clunk at full extension, too much makes the end of the stroke harsh.

records.topic: 2024 YZ250FX shock spring options and set-up after a spring change
records.statement: Yamaha lists optional shock springs from 48 to 60 N/mm in 2 N/mm steps (standard 56 N/mm) and fork springs from 4.1 to 5.1 N/mm (standard 4.6). After fitting any shock spring, reset sag to a 90-100 mm sunken (rider-on) length; with a softer spring turn rebound out 1-2 clicks, with a stiffer one turn it in 1-2 clicks, and since rebound changes affect compression feel, back compression off to correct. Recheck sag once a new spring has bedded in.
records.notes: Tuning chapter 10-3/10-4 (rear shock absorber and front fork setting parts tables, choosing set length).

records.topic: 2024 YZ250FX Power Tuner fuel and ignition changes
records.statement: Fuel and ignition can be changed without parts using Yamaha's Power Tuner smartphone app, which writes injection and ignition-timing corrections into the ECU and selects which map the handlebar mode switch calls up. A dealer diagnostic tool can show whether Power Tuner settings are stored (diagnostic codes 60 and 64) and erase all setting maps to return the ECU to stock (code 65).

diag_codes.60: EEPROM fault display incl. Power Tuner corrections

records.notes: Instrument and control functions (Power Tuner app / mode switch) and the self-diagnostic code table, chapter 9.

records.statement: Aftermarket full exhaust systems for the YZ250FX are sold as fitting the 2019-on bikes, the 2024 included (shared with the YZ250F of the same years); they are sold for closed-course competition use only and the maker gives no measured power figure.

source.name: Cycle Gear product listing, Big Gun EXO-R full system YZ250F/YZ250FX

records.notes: Fitment from the retailer listing; other makers (GPR, Yoshimura) list 2020-2024 YZ250FX systems. No 2024 FX before/after dyno found.
